title: Hydrated session protocol and SDK concessions (PRD - WIP)
content:
TL;DR: Propose a "Hydrated Session" protocol that makes hosted streaming + tool-calls robust for intermittent clients (mobile, edge) by allowing compact session snapshots, incremental hydration of state, and an ergonomic SDK surface that accepts partial responses and resolves to typed outputs. Goals: 1) Keep tail-latency small for stable clients while enabling reconnect/resume for flaky networks. 2) Support typed tool-call handshakes and deterministic replay of tool results when possible. 3) Provide easy-to-adopt SDK primitives that minimize client code and reduce server-side complexity for common patterns.

Background/context:
- We frequently hear from SDK integrators that streaming sessions are fragile for mobile apps and serverless lambdas with short-lived connections.
- Current hosted streaming works well for long-lived websockets but lacks a compact snapshot format and clear semantics for tool calls resumed after reconnect.
- Many product PRDs here focus on partial-response contracts and incremental outputs, but we lack a single, opinionated hydration story that ties session snapshots, typed tool handshakes, and SDK ergonomics together.

Non-goals:
- This document does not propose changes to server-side billing semantics. Billing/credits are out-of-scope.
- Not proposing heavy cryptographic attestations for snapshots (we'll rely on existing auth + audit logs for now).

User stories (prioritized):
- Mobile chat app reconnect: user loses network mid-stream; when they re-open the app it should resume the last coherent state and continue tool calls without confusing duplicates.
- Serverless orchestrator: short-lived lambda needs to complete a multi-step tool flow; it should prefetch possible tool outputs, persist a compact snapshot, and resume without re-running the LLM if possible.
- Low-bandwidth device: prefers a partial, typed summary first (low fidelity) then incremental hydration of attachments/large tool responses when bandwidth permits.

Design principles:
- Compactness first: snapshots should be small (kb-sized) and contain only what is necessary to continue a session.
- Typed determinism: where a tool-call is deterministic (idempotent), we include a stable tool-result fingerprint to enable safe replay or resume.
- Progressive hydration: clients can opt-in for lazy hydration of heavy payloads (attachments, embeddings, long tool outputs).
- SDK ergonomics: expose 2–3 small primitives that cover 90% of integrator needs (startSession, onPartial, hydrateSnapshot, finalize).

Protocol overview (Hydrated Session):
1) Session initialization: client calls POST /sessions with session prefs (fidelityPolicy, preferTypedResponses boolean, snapshotTTL). Server returns session_id + initial policy.
2) Streaming exchange: tokens/events streamed over websocket/HTTP2. Events are typed (TOKEN, PARTIAL_JSON, TOOL_CALL, TOOL_RESULT_REF, SNAPSHOT_POINT).
3) Snapshot point: server emits SNAPSHOT_POINT periodically or on explicit 'checkpoint' boundaries. Snapshot payload is a small object with: - session_id - stable incremental counter - client-visible state summary (text cursor, lastTypedOutputFingerprint) - tool-call ledger (list of recent tool calls with fingerprints) - hydrationHints (list of payload ids and size estimates)
4) Snapshot transfer: snapshot content is encoded as compact JSONL with base64 blobs only for tiny payloads; large payloads are stored as server-side artifacts and referenced by id. The snapshot id is a short opaque token (snapshot_ref).
5) Resume flow: client reconnects with session_id + snapshot_ref + resume_offset. Server validates snapshot_ref TTL and either: a) re-attaches the existing live session and streams the missing tokens, or b) if original runtime is gone, server performs a lightweight continuation by replaying cached KV (no full model re-run) or by issuing a guarded re-roll (flagging non-deterministic tool calls).
6) Deterministic tool replay: when tool results are deterministic and fingerprinted, server can replay the tool-result ledger instead of re-invoking tools. For non-deterministic tools, server marks ledger entries as volatile and SDK must reconcile duplicates.

SDK surface (sketch):
- startSession(opts) -> {sessionId, socketUrl, snapshotTTL}
- onEvent(callback) -> callback receives typed events: {type: "partial_text" | "json_frame" | "tool_call" | "tool_result" | "snapshot_point"} with helpful helpers to coalesce frames.
- hydrateSnapshot(snapshotRef, opts) -> returns a hydration stream for optional large payloads; SDK will do exponential backoff + bandwidth-aware streaming.
- commitSession(reason) -> request server to seal a stable snapshot for long-term storage (used by Dedicated/private customers).
- convenience: simpleResume(token) -> attempts best-effort reconnect using the latest cached snapshot and resolves to finalResponse or resumeError.

SDK ergonomic constraints and default behaviors:
- Default to conservative dedup: SDK will ignore tool-call events repeated within a 2s window unless fingerprint differs. Configurable.
- Backoff policy: snapshot hydration retries should be bandwidth-aware (use NetworkInformation API where available), defaulting to small-chunk first.
- Typed outputs: if preferTypedResponses is true, SDK should validate incoming PARTIAL_JSON frames against a provided JSON Schema and surface schema errors as events rather than throwing.
- Minimal integration: one small helper to map tool result fingerprints to application tool-handles (useful for orchestrators).

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit snapshot creation metric (snapshot.size_bytes, snapshot.storage_ms, snapshot.produced_by).
- Resume outcomes: resume_success, resume_replay_used, resume_fallback_rerun. These must be surfaced in Console per-route.
- Tool-call fidelity drift: track cases where a resumed session used tool-results vs re-invoked tool. Show as ratio per customer.

Compatibility and rollout strategy:
- Phase 0 (experimental): SDK opt-in flag and server-side feature gate for sessions. No change to default sessions.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable for power customers; provide migration guide. Allow Dedicated/Private customers to configure snapshot TTL and storage.
- Phase 2 (default): flip on for hosted streaming with conservative defaults; monitor telemetry and provide a one-click console toggle.

Security & privacy notes:
- Snapshots contain minimal PII by default; teams must opt-in to include attachments. Snapshot encryption at rest is mandatory; in Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS.
- Snapshot refs expire after snapshotTTL; default 24h for hosted. Dedicated customers can configure up to 30d.

Operational considerations / cost implications:
- Snapshot storage: small per-snapshot charge. We must add a visibility row in billing.
- Cache pressure: server retains recent snapshots in fast cache for quick resume; need eviction policy tuned by session activity.

Open questions / tradeoffs (needs triage):
- Where to draw line between replaying tool-results vs re-invoking? (safety vs cost). Proposal: conservative replay for idempotent tools only; for external side-effect tools require explicit allow_replay flag.
- How to handle authenticated tool-calls that rely on ephemeral credentials? Snapshot cannot store secrets; we must provide a replay token that signals the client must re-authorize certain tool invocations on resume.
- Schema evolution for typed outputs: introduce "schema_version" in snapshots and provide SDK helper to migrate old schemas. Complexity vs benefit?

Backward-compat checklist for the eng teams:
- [ ] server: produce SNAPSHOT_POINT events and snapshot_ref API endpoint (storage + TTL).
- [ ] runtime: add tool-call ledger fingerprints and deterministic flag.
- [ ] console: surface snapshot metrics and per-route resume telemetry.
- [ ] SDK: implement lightweight resume helper, hydration API, and dedup heuristics.
- [ ] docs: migration guide + examples for mobile + serverless.

Next steps (short term):
- Product to align on deterministic replay policy (owners: Ava, Diego). Target decision by 2025-03-10.
- Eng spike: prototype snapshot encoding + QoS-aware hydrate flow (owner: Marcus). 2 week spike.
- UX/SDK: draft minimal APIs and compatibility tests (owner: Priya). 1 sprint for initial SDK patch.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a high-level PRD sketch, intentionally light on exact wire proto. Looking for feedback on: snapshot TTL defaults, replay safety model, and the minimum viable SDK primitives.

Quick links and references:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1482 (streaming snapshot proposals)
- Jira: JIRA-API-782 (snapshot infra task)
- Github: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/394 (initial resume prototype)

Handy friction log / TODOs (brainstorm-y):
- client-side storage format examples (localStorage vs secure store)
- attachment watermarking for long-lived snapshots (privacy)
- test harness for flaky reconnection scenarios (capture sequences of events + expected dedup behaviour)

Bottom line: Hydrated Session is an opinionated medium-sized feature that buys resilience for mobile and serverless customers while keeping the streaming fast-path unchanged. If we agree on a conservative replay policy and a tiny SDK surface, this should be adoptable incrementally by customers and low-risk to roll out.
